specification.problem: Approximate a given single-qubit unitary U to precision epsilon with a Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) circuit over Clifford+T plus one ancilla and measurement, minimizing expected T-count. The abstract claims a probabilistically polynomial-time classical synthesis algorithm, but gives no construction.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the generic RUS success/failure structure and the T-count comparison with the ancilla-free bound 3 log2(1/epsilon) are specified. The paper's actual synthesis algorithm (how the RUS circuit is found, the polynomial-time method, the numerics) is outside this scope.

symbols.meaning: Clifford+T circuit acting on data qubit and one ancilla
2x2 operator on the data qubit applied upon the success measurement outcome (ancilla |0>)
unitary implemented on success, K_0 up to normalization

equations.label: Ancilla-free T-count lower bound
equations.description: Theoretical lower bound for ancilla-free single-qubit Clifford+T decomposition quoted in the abstract.
equations.abstract_quote: theoretical lower bound of $3\log_{2}(1/\varepsilon)$ for ancilla-free single-qubit circuit decomposition
equations.justification: Stated directly in the abstract as a bound.
assumptions: Asymptotic/leading-order meaning; additive constants not given

equations.label: Reported expected T-count ratio
equations.description: Numerical average claim: RUS expected T-count is about 2.5 times lower than the ancilla-free bound.
equations.abstract_quote: expected $T$-count on average $2.5$ times lower than the theoretical lower bound
equations.justification: Inferred by translating the 2.5 times lower claim into a ratio. It is an empirical average, not an exact equality.

equations.label: RUS attempt structure
equations.description: Success branch of one attempt: measuring the ancilla in |0> applies K_0 to the data qubit. Ideally K_0 = sqrt(p) times a unitary close to U.
equations.justification: Generic RUS structure; the abstract names RUS with one ancilla and measurement but gives no explicit W or K_0.
assumptions: K_0 proportional to a unitary independent of psi

equations.label: Approximation condition
equations.description: Precision requirement on the success-branch unitary.
equations.justification: The abstract states approximation within epsilon but not the norm. The operator norm is assumed (global phase handling unspecified).
assumptions: Operator norm or a comparable metric

equations.label: Expected T-count with geometric repetition
equations.description: If each attempt costs T_a T gates and succeeds independently with probability p, the number of attempts is geometric with mean 1/p. Failure branches are assumed correctable or restartable at no extra cost.
equations.justification: Standard geometric-trial expectation; the paper's actual cost model is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Failures restart cleanly without extra T cost
Constant T_a and p across attempts

registers.name: data
registers.role: qubit on which the approximation of U is implemented

registers.name: ancilla
registers.role: ancilla measured to herald success or failure

specification.initial_state: Assumed: ancilla |0> and data in an arbitrary state |psi>.

steps.description: Prepare ancilla in |0> and apply the Clifford+T circuit W on data and ancilla (the specific W is not given in the abstract).
Measure the ancilla. On the success outcome the data holds K_0|psi>/sqrt(p), approximating U. On failure, correct or restart, repeating until success.
Compare the expected T-count with the ancilla-free bound.

specification.measurement: Ancilla measured in the computational basis after each attempt; the success outcome is assumed to be 0.
specification.classical_postprocessing: The classical probabilistic polynomial-time synthesis search that finds W for given U and epsilon is not specified in the abstract.
assumptions: Failure branches are handled by restarting, with no extra cost.
The error metric is the operator norm.
No explicit tiny instance is chosen because the construction is unknown.
